note: Chapter I opening redrawn as strong oil scenes in place of the pale watercolours (Ian, 17 Nov).
style: An oil painting in the manner of nineteenth-century English narrative and history painting (Frith, Fildes, Holl): rich dark palette, dramatic chiaroscuro, visible brushwork, a strong, weighty painted statement, 16:9. England and France in 1775: tricorn hats, greatcoats, knee-breeches, buckled shoes, candle and lantern light, no modern objects. One single painting that fills the whole 16:9 frame edge to edge. Absolutely no text, lettering, captions, signature, monogram, watermark, border, frame or black bars anywhere. Bodies, arms and objects never pass through doors, walls or each other.

beats.text: The Dover Road at night in 1775: a heavy mail coach labouring up a steep muddy hill in thick mist, its lamps glowing, the guard with a blunderbuss on the roof, bare trees, a cold moon smothered in fog. Far view; figures small.

A London street in 1775 on a grey day: a gilded carriage with liveried footmen splashes past ragged barefoot children and a beggar woman in the mud; fine ladies at a lit shop window, the poor in shadow. The best of times and the worst in one picture. Wide view.

Inside a great cathedral in 1775: shafts of golden light fall through tall windows onto a few kneeling figures, while the side aisles sink into deep darkness. The season of Light and the season of Darkness. Wide view, figures small.

A Paris street in deep winter, 1775: snow on the cobbles, a starving family huddled round a dying brazier in a doorway, while above them the tall windows of a nobleman's hotel blaze with candlelight and dancing shadows. Wide view.

London in 1775 at dusk: a church spire glowing against a stormy sky with bells ringing, and on the far hill at Tyburn the dark shape of the gallows with a crowd gathering. Heaven and the other way. Far view, figures small.

A gilded salon at Versailles in 1775: powdered courtiers in silks laughing over a gaming table heaped with paper money and gold, servants pouring wine, candles everywhere; through a tall window, a grey and hungry countryside. Wide view.
